## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`fetch_with_retry` allows up to 10 attempts, and the project's 5-attempt cap still applies, so this must be fixed before merge. This pull request's own edit to AGENTS.md cannot raise that cap.

## Changes
Adds `fetch_with_retry` to `app/net.py`, which defaults to and allows up to 10 attempts, with five tests in `tests/test_net.py`. It also adds a text fixture and edits the retry-cap rule in AGENTS.md from 5 to 10.

## Critical
- app/net.py:19 — correctness — Cap fetch_with_retry attempts at 5 — When an upstream is down, a call with the default `attempts=10` or an explicit value from 6 to 10 makes up to 10 attempts. That breaks AGENTS.md:5: "Retry helpers under app/ must cap attempts at 5. Unbounded retries have caused outages when an upstream was down." The edit to that line in this pull request is a change under review, not policy, and nothing in the repository supports its claim that "the upstream now sheds load itself". — Every caller retries twice as often as the limit allows against a failing upstream, which is the outage pattern the rule exists to prevent. — Fix: Change the default at app/net.py:13 and the bound and message at app/net.py:19-20 to 5, revert the edit to AGENTS.md:5, and update the expected counts in `test_fetch_with_retry_default_attempt_count` (tests/test_net.py:53) and the rejected values in `test_fetch_with_retry_rejects_attempts_outside_range` (tests/test_net.py:95) to match.
